## What the source says

This prospective study followed 25 Japanese people with type 2 diabetes taking oral semaglutide over three months. It assessed dietary intake and body-composition measures. Its small size, population and formulation limit generalisation; it does not prove muscle preservation for people using other semaglutide products.

## Evidence and limits

The study followed 25 Japanese adults with type 2 diabetes for three months, using dietary questionnaires, bioimpedance measurements and handgrip testing. The authors reported body-weight and dietary changes and a higher percentage of muscle mass, with no significant handgrip change. A percentage is not proof that absolute muscle mass or strength was preserved.

## What we checked

We checked the primary publication record and available abstract. The full paper and supplements have not been reviewed for this correction.
